description: A button that pulls like a slingshot; releasing flings the pad out of its seat and scatters particles.
interactionNotes: Drag the button; the band stretches and the power arc fills. Once you pass the arming threshold, releasing launches it: the pad leaves its seat, particles spread in a cone, and then it returns. If you release before it arms, it springs back and sends nothing. A simple tap also sends (if `tapSends` is on), and Enter and Space always do.

props.children: The content of the pad. Defaults to an up arrow.
props.onSend: Called when releasing while armed, on a tap (if `tapSends` is on), and on Enter or Space.
props.accentColor: The power arc, the arming band and the launch point.
props.wellColor: The seat the pad rests on.
props.size: Pad diameter, px. The seat, hit area and launch point scale with it too.
props.strokeWidth: Thickness of the arc and band, px. The band gets thinner as it stretches.
props.armAt: The distance at which the shot arms, px.
props.maxPull: How far the band stretches before it stops giving, px.
props.launchSpeed: The speed the band adds on release, px/s. It determines how far past the seat the pad travels.
props.recoil: Bounce of the return spring; zero means no bounce.
props.flight: How far the leading point travels, px; the rest scatter around it.
props.particles: Number of launch particles. Each gets a random angle, range, size, drift, speed and delay. 1 means a single dot, zero means none.
props.spread: The cone the burst spreads within, in degrees, around the launch direction.
props.axis: Free dragging, or one axis with a little play on the other axis.
props.tapSends: Whether a simple tap also sends; Enter always sends.
props.disabled: Dims the pad and ignores input.
props.autoPreview: Site preview only: it performs the pull, arm and release itself so the flight, the particles and the elastic return can be seen along the real path.

tips: Dragging without releasing sends nothing — it doesn't arm until you pass `armAt`, and `onSend` isn't called.
`armAt` and `maxPull` work together: the first says where it arms, the second caps the pull. If you bring `armAt` close to `maxPull`, the user has to pull all the way to fire.
For a "send" button, set `armAt` at least larger than `size` so the arming motion extends beyond the pad and stays visible.
Lower `recoil` (e.g. 0.05) for a dry, technical feel; raising it (near 0.3) makes the button more playful.
This component shows no feedback of its own; handle `onSend` and add your own message or state (the site demo does this with a "Sent" label).
Turn on `disabled` while sending so the user doesn't launch again.

Set `particles` to zero if you want the pad to fly out without a burst; `spread` only matters when there are particles. `axis` only constrains the drag axis, not the launch — the launch is always along the drag direction.
